notes: Both from the Census Bureau API (2000 SF1 P001001 = 'Total' under TOTAL POPULATION; 2020 PL P1_001N = 'Total:' under RACE). The API now requires a key (keyless calls 302 to a Missing Key page); calls were made with the Keychain CENSUS_API_KEY, which is stripped from the URLs above. Growth 2000-2020: +795,912 (+9.9%).

item: Total population (latest Census Bureau estimate, Vintage 2025, July 1, 2025)
now_quote: New York City's population declined by 12,196 between 2024 and 2025, the greatest numeric decrease in the nation.
notes: Census press release dated 'For Immediate Release: Thursday, May 14, 2026'; its Table 5 row reads 'New York city New York 8,584,629'. NYC DCP's July 2026 PDF (text extracted locally with pypdf) carries the same 8,584,629 for July 2025 and notes Vintage 2025 revised the July 2024 figure upward 'from 8,478,000 to 8,597,000'. City is 219,561 below the April 2020 count but 576,351 above the 2000 count.

2000 share computed: 2,871,032 / 8,008,278 = 35.85%. Variable labels verified from https://api.census.gov/data/2000/dec/sf3/variables.json (P021013 = 'Total!!Foreign born', PLACE OF BIRTH BY CITIZENSHIP STATUS) and https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/profile/variables.json (DP02_0094PE = 'Percent!!PLACE OF BIRTH!!Total population!!Foreign-born'). 2023 ACS 1-year was 37.5% / 3,093,845 (same call against /data/2023/). Note the ACS 2024 total population base is 8,478,072 (the pre-revision Vintage 2024 estimate), so the count is on a smaller base than the census.

item: Race/ethnicity shares (non-Hispanic white, Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic Asian)
notes: Shares computed from the counts over each census total. Variable labels verified: 2000 SF1 P008010 = 'Total!!Hispanic or Latino', P008003 = 'Total!!Not Hispanic or Latino!!White alone', P008004 = '...Black or African American alone', P008006 = '...Asian alone'; 2020 PL P2_002N = Hispanic or Latino, P2_005N/P2_006N/P2_008N = Not Hispanic, one race, White/Black/Asian alone. Asian alone (non-Hispanic) grew 76% (780,229 to 1,373,502); Black alone (non-Hispanic) fell by 185,263. For a more recent read, ACS 2024 1-year (https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/profile?get=NAME,DP05_0090PE,DP05_0096PE,DP05_0097PE,DP05_0099PE&for=place:51000&in=state:36) returned ["New York city, New York","28.7","30.7","20.0","15.1","36","51000"] = Hispanic 28.7%, NH white 30.7%, NH Black 20.0%, NH Asian 15.1%. Caution: 2020 census race data are not strictly comparable with 2000 because of question-design changes (more multiracial responses), which is part of why 'alone' categories fell.

P053001 label verified as 'Median household income in 1999' (Census 2000 SF3, collected in 2000 for calendar 1999). DP03_0062E verified as 'Median household income (dollars)' in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars. Nominal figures; not inflation-adjusted to each other. 2023 ACS 1-year value was $76,577.

2000 SF1 P013001 verified as 'Median age!!Both sexes'. 2024 ACS DP05_0018E verified as 'Median age (years)'. 2020 census (DHC P13_001N) gave 36.8; 2023 ACS 1-year gave 38.8. So the city has aged about four years.

H001001 verified as 'Total' under HOUSING UNITS (2000 SF1); DP04_0001E verified as 'Total housing units' (ACS 2024). The 2020 census count (DHC H1_001N, https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/dhc?get=NAME,P1_001N,P13_001N,H1_001N,P12_001N&for=place:51000&in=state:36) returned 3,618,635. Census-to-census 2000-2020: +417,723 (+13.0%). 2000 vs 2024 ACS: +536,720 (+16.8%), though ACS and decennial counts are different instruments.

2000 count is the sum of eight SF1 SEX BY AGE cells (male and female: Under 5, 5 to 9, 10 to 14, 15 to 17), labels verified from the SF1 variables.json; share = 1,940,269 / 8,008,278. 2024 ACS DP05_0019E/PE verified as 'Under 18 years' count and percent. Children fell by about 280,000 while the total population grew; a big shift the infographic could feature.

then_quote: Over the past decade (2001–2010), overall LE at birth in NYC increased 3 years from 77.9 to 80.9 years.
now_quote: New Yorkers' life expectancy rose from 80.7 in 2021 to 83.2 years in 2024 — an increase of 2.5 years.
notes: 2001 figure: NYC DOHMH Epi Research Report, March 2013 (PDF text extracted locally with pypdf; the PDF's text has spaces stripped, so the quote is re-spaced but otherwise verbatim). Corroborated by the Dec. 11, 2012 Mayor's Office chart PDF (Bureau of Vital Statistics series starting '77.9 78.2 78.5 ...' for 2001-2010) and by the PubMed abstract at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25887941/ ('NYC residents' life expectancy at birth increased from 77.9 years (95% CI, 77.8-78.0) in 2001'). 2024 figure is labeled PROVISIONAL in the Nov. 20, 2025 NYC Health release ('New Yorkers' provisional 2024 life expectancy rose to 83.2 years'); the last final figure is 82.6 for 2023, per the same release ('This has surpassed the high of 82.6 years from 2019 and 2023.'). Gain of 5.3 years 2001 to 2024.
